title.narrative: Building Resilience through Social and Emotional Learning: Education Recovery for Children in Gaza and the West Bank

description.narrative:
Context For more than 56 years, Palestine faces a protracted protection and political crisis characterized by military occupation, 16 years of the Gaza blockade, internal Palestinian divisions, lack of adherence to international humanitarian and human rights law, and recurrent escalations of hostilities. The latest round of hostilities which commenced in October 2023 is ongoing and has resulted in unprecedented levels of destruction and suffering. After a brief ceasefire and a temporary easing of basic goods entry into Gaza, all crossings for incoming cargo were completely closed on March 3rd, 2025. Starting in the early hours of March 18th, airstrikes resumed across the Gaza Strip, leading to further civilian casualties, mass displacement, and significant worsening of humanitarian conditions.
Ninety per cent of Gaza’s current population of 2.1 million people has been displaced, lacking access to sufficient shelter, food, life-saving medical services, clean water, education and livelihoods. The education system is facing a near-total collapse, with 95.2% of educational infrastructure severely damaged, resulting in significant disruptions to the learning of 658,000 students. The impact has not only been physical but also psychological, with children facing high levels of trauma, emotional distress, and psychological issues due to prolonged exposure to violence. 17 months of missed schooling have led to substantial learning losses, particularly in foundational literacy and numeracy among children. In many cases, Temporary Learning Spaces (TLSs) have been the only option, accommodating just 25% of school-aged children. Furthermore, war-related disabilities, life-changing injuries, and heightened mental health challenges have created barriers not just to learning but to social reintegration and emotional recovery.
Since October 2023, Palestinians in the West Bank have faced intensified restrictions due to discriminatory planning regime. Restrictions have included prolonged checkpoint delays, closure of town entrances and blockage of secondary roads. As a result, 782,000 students have experienced school closures, settler violence, demolitions, and military operations, severely disrupting their education and sense of security.
The northern West Bank, specifically Tulkarm city and its refugee camps have been significantly affected by Israeli military operations. These operations have been ongoing for over a few months, leading to mass displacement and the near desertion of refugee camps. The military operations are part of a larger-scale operation in the northern West Bank, which also includes Jenin and Nablus. These operations have intensified restrictions, caused displacement, and disrupted access to education and basic services.
To address the scale of learning loss and the psychological toll of prolonged conflict and displacement, the Education Cluster and the INEE Accelerated Education Working Group recommend that all education interventions systematically integrate mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) and social and emotional learning (SEL). Creating inclusive, caring, and safe learning environments is essential, not only to facilitate the return to education but also to restore a sense of normalcy, build resilience, and support emotional healing. SEL should be embedded across curricula, teaching practices, and school environments, equipping both learners and teachers with the tools to cope with adversity. This includes providing targeted teacher training to recognize and respond to signs of distress, and establishing referral systems in coordination with the Protection Cluster to ensure access to specialized support services. Prioritizing MHPSS and SEL is not optional, it is foundational to any sustainable recovery and to enabling Palestinian learners to reclaim their right to education.
Overall goal To establish inclusive, safe, and supportive learning environments that integrate Learning SEL and MHPSS as foundational components, enabling Palestinian learners and educators to recover from adversity, rebuild resilience, and regain their right to quality education
Activities 1. Deliver a 30-week SEL programme through existing Temporary Learning Spaces (TLSs) and families in Gaza, as well as schools in the West Bank. Which shall support the continuation of learning in safe, inclusive, and accessible environments for the levels KG2 to Grade 4. 2. Expand learning offered to all children (KG2-Grade 4) to include SEL (in addition to literacy and numeracy) 3. Provide comprehensive training for caregivers, teachers, supervisors, and MoEHE leadership to enhance their competencies in TE SEL and trauma-informed practices 4. Institutionalize TE SEL programme within the education system to ensure long-term implementation and resilience. 5. Integrate TE SEL indicators into the MoEHE’s M&E system for regular tracking of student progress.
Deliverables 1. Conducive learning environment available at KGs, basic schools, and TLSs 2. 475,000 children equipped with socio-emotional competencies. 3. 9,500 teachers trained to effectively deliver TE SEL content. 4.Crises affected Palestinian children attaining improved quality learning that includes SEL. 5. KG caregivers and basic schoolteachers qualified in TE trauma-informed SEL program delivery 6. 400 MoEHE supervisors trained as master trainers to support SEL implementation. 7. MoEHE school principals and Ministry and senior staff oriented on Think Equal (TE) SEL programme. 8. Children's social and emotional skills assessed and reported through the MoEHE’s M&E report 9. SEL program institutionalized within the Palestinian education system
